title: Williams Makes a Nine and Wins Anyway: The Spoon-Holder Takes the Trophy
title_candidates: Williams Makes a Nine and Wins Anyway: The Spoon-Holder Takes the Trophy
Spoon to Trophy: Williams by Two, Mullin by Miles and by Nothing
Nine Ways to Lose by Two: Baker's Algarve Arithmetic
The Boavista Record Falls, and So Does the Champion
theme: Both the record book and the pecking order turned over in the Algarve: the reigning Wooden Spoon holder won the Trophy by two, the defending champion rewrote Boavista's record book and then unravelled into last place — and wherever you looked, somebody was writing another 9 on the card.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, insider-facing; ribbing but never fabricated
opening_hook: Open on R4 at Palmares, Williams standing over a 9 at the 16th (b13) and still winning the Trophy by two (b02) — then loop back to how a man who arrived as reigning Wooden Spoon holder got into that position at all.
foreshadow: Williams arrives as reigning Wooden Spoon holder (TEG 4), Jacket rank 5th in each of the last three TEGs, no Trophy wins — the least likely man in the field
Mullin arrives as defending Trophy champion with back-to-back Jackets, and Boavista's 35-visit gross record is about to be his
Baker's scorecards keep sprouting single holes of 8 and 9 while the Trophy margin stays tiny
Nobody has ever seen Palmares — a brand-new course as the final-day leveller

competitions.name: Trophy (Net VP)
competitions.winner_or_loser: Gregg Williams (winner, -6, by 2 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Mullin led after R1 (by 1) and R2 (by 3), Williams sitting 3rd then 2nd. Williams's personal-best -6 in R2 (b09) closed the gap to 3 despite a 9 at the 8th and a 7 at the 14th; at R3 H3 a par at the par-5 (net -2) took him outright ahead of Mullin, ending 21 holes of Mullin leadership (b01/b10) — the only lead change of the tournament that mattered. He stretched to 5 by the end of R3 and, on a Palmares he had never seen, bled 10 shots over holes 10-13 and made a 9 at the 16th (b13) yet still came home in -1 and won by 2, because Baker was busy running up an 8 at the 5th (b20).

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.winner_or_loser: David Mullin (winner, +72, by 12 from Jon Baker)
competitions.how: Decided almost before it began: Mullin went to the front on gross at R1 H3 — the only Jacket lead change all tournament — and his +12 at Boavista (b03), the best gross round in TEG history to date, opened an 8-shot cushion. R2's +11 (b04) equalled that record and made it 14; the 82 gross broke Boavista's course record of 85, standing across 35 prior visits (cr01). A +27 in R3 and +22 at Palmares were untidy but irrelevant: the margin never dipped below 12.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: For two rounds Mullin was the last man anyone expected here: -3 then -4, leading the Trophy. Neumann held bottom place through R1's routine shuffling, Meller took it at R2 H3 and sat there through R3. Then Mullin posted +12 net in R3, his worst round to date (b21), including a 9 at the 13th (b30), and fell to 4th. At Palmares a 9 at the 6th put him bottom for the first time (b22/b31); Meller's double bogey at the 15th briefly took it back (b23); and at the 17th — a par on the easiest hole on the course, SI 18 — Mullin dropped to the bottom for the last time (b24) while Meller was completing a personal-best round (b14/b15). Spoon to the Jacket winner (b25).

rounds.chosen_headline: Palmares, First Acquaintance: Williams Makes a 9 at the 16th and Still Wins by Two
rounds.angle: A course nobody had played decides all three: Williams bleeds through 10-13, makes a 9 at the 16th and comes home in -1 to win by 2 (b13/b02); Baker's personal-best gross +18 (b11) is undone by an 8 at the 5th (b20); Mullin's 9 at the 6th and par at the 17th hand him the Spoon (b22/b24/b25) on the day he seals the Jacket by 12 (b05), while Meller escapes with a personal best (b14/b15).

players.arc: Reigning Wooden Spoon holder and dead last on gross in each of the previous three TEGs, he posted a personal-best -6 in R2, took the Trophy lead with a par at R3's 3rd and held it to the end — winning his first Trophy at -6 by two despite a 9 at Palmares' 16th.

The defending champion rewrote TEG's gross best twice and broke a 35-visit Boavista course record, then went +12 and +7 in net terms to walk off with the Green Jacket by 12 and the Wooden Spoon in the same pair of hands.

Runner-up in both the Trophy and the Jacket, two shots and twelve shots short respectively, having donated four separate holes of 8 or 9 across the tournament — including one at Palmares' 5th on the day he shot a personal-best gross.
Author of the best net round in TEG history to date (-9) and an 82 gross that matched a brand-new course record — then a 9 at Boavista's 18th in R3 to remind everyone he was here.
Two prior Spoons and holder of the bottom slot from R2 H3 through R3, he escaped only at Palmares, where a personal-best -3 (and personal-best +17 gross) passed the parcel to Mullin.

venue_notes: TEG's 3rd visit to the Algarve, June 2012. Rounds 1-3 at Boavista (Howard Swan parkland above Lagos, Atlantic views, two distinct halves) are the 8th, 9th and 10th TEG rounds at the venue — the most familiar ground in the tournament's short history, which is what makes the record-breaking of R2 land. R4 moves to Palmares (Robert Trent Jones Jr., 27 holes of parkland, lakeside and links; the Lagos/Praia combination), a new course for TEG and unseen by all five — use it as the final-day leveller that decided the Trophy margin and the Spoon. Weekday references, if any, only from the schedule: R1 Sunday, R4 Wednesday.
course_history_notes: Boavista's gross record of 85 had stood across 35 prior visits; it fell in R2 to Mullin's 82 (cr01) — and Neumann signed for 82 the same round, a 7-shot personal best at the venue.
Improvement was collective at Boavista: Mullin 9 shots better than his last visit, Neumann 12 better, Baker and Williams 8 better each.
Meller's Boavista best of 89 (TEG 3) survived — 91 in R3 was as close as he got — before he found his form on unfamiliar ground at Palmares.
Palmares was a first visit for all five: R4 gross of 89 (Meller), 90 (Baker), 94 (Mullin), 96 (Neumann), 104 (Williams).
decisive_moments: Trophy: R3 H3 at Boavista — Williams's par at the par-5 (net -2) ends Mullin's 21-hole spell in front (b01/b10) and he is never headed across the remaining 33 holes.
Green Jacket: R1 H3 at Boavista — Mullin goes to the front on gross in the tournament's only Jacket lead change, and his record +12 (b03) makes it an 8-shot cushion by nightfall, 14 by the end of R2.

Wooden Spoon: R4 H17 at Palmares — a par on the easiest hole on the course (SI 18) drops Mullin to the bottom for the final time (b24), the +12 in R3 (b21) and the 9 at the 6th (b31) having done the actual damage.

payoffs.seed: Baker's cards keep sprouting 8s and 9s while the Trophy margin stays tiny
payoffs.payoff: Four blow-ups of 8 or worse (b17, b18, b19, b20) against a final deficit of two: any one of them cleaned up and Baker has a second Trophy.

payoffs.seed: Palmares, a course nobody had seen, waiting on the final day
payoffs.payoff: The new course settles everything — Williams's 9 at the 16th survives (b13), Baker and Meller post personal bests (b11, b14/b15), and Mullin's 9 at the 6th starts the slide to the Spoon.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Two outright Trophy leaders is real, but Mullin faded out of contention rather than duelling to the wire — the close finish (margin 2) is Baker's four blow-ups against Williams's 9 at the 16th, so counterfactual leads, with the career inversion (Spoon holder up, champion down to last) riding alongside.
